answer: Use memory-hard proof-of-work puzzles bound to each public key. To register, an agent must solve a puzzle seeded by its key and the current epoch hash, needing 2 GB of RAM and about ten minutes of compute on a dune of commodity cores. Verifiers check a short proof in milliseconds. Credentials expire every week, so each fake must re-solve. Basalt-hard memory limits parallelism, so a sonnet-length batch of hundreds of keys needs hundreds of machines, costing roughly two dollars of rented compute per identity weekly.
